spans.s: Vāta^1 = Vāyu, q.v.--Do.^2 = Śiva (1000 names^2).
Vātādhipa, a king. § 281 (Sahadeva): II, 31, 1120 (in the south, vanquished by Sahadeva on his digvijaya).
Vātaghna, a son of Viśvāmitra. § 721b (Viśvāmitrop.): XIII, 4, 253.
Vātaja (?), pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 362 (Vātajāmarathoragāḥ; PCR. “the Vātagas (!), the Amarathas, and the Uragas”); BR. suggests VātajāmaRathoragāḥ).
Vātapati, a Vṛshṇi prince. § 232 (Svayaṃvarap.): I, 18, 7000 (came to the svayaṃvara of Draupadī).

Vātāpi or Vātāpin, an Asura, younger brother of Īlvala. § 11 (Anukram.): I, 2, 442 (ºbhakshaṇaṃ).--§ 93 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 65, 2537 (ºī, nom., among the sons of Danu).--[§ 316 (Kirmīravadhap.): III, 11, 422 (sambhakshya jarayishyāmi yathā 'gastyo mahāsuraṃ, all. to § 382)].--§ 382 (Agastyop.): III, 96, 8541, 8543, 8547 (mesharūpī), 8549 (Asuraṃ), 8551 (mahāsuraḥ); 99, 8616, 8617 (mahāsuraṃ), 8620, 8622, 8645 (Prahrādiḥ) (Ilvala used to kill brahmans by offering them V. transformed to a ram as food and again recalling him to life, but Agastya totally digested him).--§ 389 (Tīrthayātrāp.): III, 109, 9967 (ºiś ca yathā nītaḥ kshayaṃ, all. to § 382).-§ 479 (Pativratop.): III, 206, 13679 (Agastyaṃ samāsādya jīrṇaḥ…mahāsuraḥ, all. to § 382).--§ 547 (Karṇa): III, 303, 17014 (mahāsuraḥ/nihato Brahmadaṇḍena, all. to § 382).--§ 612 (Hradapraveśap.): IX, 31, 1755.--§ 649 (Āpaddh.): XII, 141, 5389 (Agastyenāsuro jagdho Vºiḥ, all. to § 382). Cf. Asura, Daitya, Ditinandana, Prāhrādi.
Vātaraṃhas = Śiva (1000 names^2).
Vātasārathi = Agni, q.v. Add: III, 10647.
Vātaskandha, a ṛshi. § 266 (Śakrasabhāv.): II, 7, 295 (in the palace of Indra).
Vātātmaja (“the son of the Wind”) = Bhīmasena: V, 5582; VIII, †4559 (Bhīmaḥ).
Vātavega^1, son of Dhṛtarāshṭra. § 130 (Aṃśāvat.): I, 67, 2737.--§ 182 (Dhṛtarāshṭhraputranāmak.): I, 117, 4549.--§ 608 (Karṇap.): VIII, 51, 2447; 84,, 4263 (slain by Bhīmasena).
Vātavega^2, a Suparṇa, son of Garuḍa. § 564 (Mātalīyop.) V, 101, 3595.
Vātāyana, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9, 363 (only C., B. has Vanāyavaḥ).
Vātika, a warrior of Skanda. § 615u (Skanda): IX, 45, 2569.
Vātika, pl. (ºāḥ) (“aerial beings”): VII, 6132 (SiddhaCāraṇa-vºaiḥ, only C., B. has -ºPannagaiḥ), 7188 (SiddhaCāraṇa-vºāḥ); IX, 3090 (ºāś Cāraṇāḥ), 3307 (º-Cāraṇāḥ).
Vātikakhaṇḍa (ºshaṇḍa, B.), name of a place. § 410 (Plakshāvataraṇag.): III, 130, 10548 (Nīl. tākes v. as an appellative = vātanītaḥ padmādisamūhaḥ).
Vatsa^1, a prince, son of the Kāśi king Pratardana. § 638b (Rāmopākhyāna): XII, 49, 1795 (Pratardanasya putraḥ, brought up among calves (vatsaiḥ). in a cowpen).
Vatsa^2, a prince, the ancestor of the Vatsas(?). § 736b (Vītahavyop.): XIII, 30, 1946 (father of Haihaya and Tālajaṅgha of Śaryāti's race).

Vatsa, pl. (ºāḥ), a people. § 573 (Ambop.): V, 186, 7369. --§ 578 (Bhīshmavadhap.): VI, 50, 2084 (in the army of Yudhishṭhira).--§ 604 (Karṇap.): VIII, 8, 237 (had formerly been vanquished by Karṇa). Cf. Vātsya, pl.

Vatsabhūmi (“the country of the Vatsas”). § 280 (Bhīmasena): II, 30, 1084 (in the east, conquered by Bhīmasena on his digvijaya).--§ 515 (Karṇadigvijaya): III, 254, 15243 (conquered by Karṇa).--§ 561 (Yānasandhip.): V, 53, 2107 (ºpān, in the army of Yudhishṭhira).--§ 573 (Ambopākhyānap.): V, 186, 7351 (Siddha-Cāraṇasevitāṃ), 7366, 7367 (Ambā, with half her body, became transformed to the river of that name in V.).
Vatsala^1, a warrior of Skanda. § 615u (Skanda): IX, 45, 2574.--Do.^2 = Vishṇu (1000 names).
Vatsara = Vishṇu (1000 names).
Vatsarāja (“the king of the Vatsas”). § 232 (Svayaṃvarap.): I, 186, 7002 (came to the svayaṃvara of Draupadī).
Vatsin = Vishṇu (1000 names).
Vātsya, name of one or more brahmans. § 59 (Sarpasattra): I, 53, 2049 (among the sadasyas at the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya).--§ 637 (Rājadh.): XII, 47, 1592 (among those who surrounded Bhīshma).

Vātsya, pl. (ºāḥ), a people = Vatsa, pl. § 589 (Droṇābhishekap.): VII, 11, 396 (º-Gārgya-Karūshān, had formerly been vanquished by Kṛshṇa).--§ 736b (Vītahavyop.): XIII, 30, 1951 (ºānāṃ, sc. purīṃ; = the Haihayas(?); reading of C. Vatsyānāṃ, B. Vatsānāṃ)
